messages:
elaine_s: Quick customer ask — AcmeCorp POC. They want outbound IPs to rotate daily (security policy) but their firewall team will only allow 3 IPs total. They don't want to request more static EIPs. Can we support a flow that satisfies both?

michael_nw: Short answer: there are 3 realistic patterns we can propose. Longer notes below.

michael_nw: 1) Dedicated endpoint + small reserved pool (stable CIDR/EIP) — easiest for firewall allowlisting. We can provide 1-3 static EIPs per dedicated pool. Rotation = painful for their firewall.

michael_nw: 2) Use a reverse-proxy/SNI fronting approach — we route many backend IPs but present a stable hostname via SNI. If their FW can allow by hostname (rare) or by an intermediate proxy they control, that works. Needs TLS termination strategy.

michael_nw: 3) Private/VPC option — VPC peering or Private deployment avoids public egress constraints entirely. Best for enterprise but heavier setup for POC.

elaine_s: They explicitly said "no long procurement for EIPs" but rotating IPs is a hard requirement. Any hybrid?

michael_nw: Hybrid: we can do a short-lived dedicated pool (marketing/demo reserve) and rotate which pool is presented to the customer daily while keeping a tiny stable control IP for auth/health checks. But their firewall still needs the rotate range or they must accept a small CIDR instead of specific IPs. Recommend asking FW to allow a /29 or /28 rather than single IPs.

devon_sec: Security checklist notes:
- Provide rotation schedule and TTL for IPs.
- TLS cipher suites we use and cert chain (we can produce cert bundle).
- Support for mTLS on Dedicated (we can enable mutual TLS per endpoint) — that avoids IP-only allowlist work.
- Audit logs: we can export request logs for the sessions.

devon_sec: If they want rotation + strict allowlist, mTLS is the best compromise: we present a short-lived client cert, they only allow connections from our pool, and auth is still cert-based.

sasha_reqs: Pricing/ops question from AE: Is there an additional setup charge for provisioning static EIPs for a short POC? Also what do we need from the customer to configure SNI proxying?

michael_nw: For short POCs we can usually waive infra setup fees — coordinate with finance. Technically we need:
- list of allowed CIDR(s) they will open (if any)
- desired hostname for SNI (if using proxy) and SAN on certs
- whether they want mTLS + their CA bundle (or we issue client certs)
- test API key for POC and expected qps/latency profile

michael_nw: Quick test curl we recommend for them once allowlist is set:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_API_KEY" \
  https://dedicated-usw1.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"hi"}'
```

elaine_s: FW team asked about ephemeral IP rotation details they can include in the SQA. Can you paste the rotation cadence and who to ping if a connection drops?

devon_sec: Rotation cadence: daily by default for this POC unless they request hourly. We will publish a signed JWT-based rotation manifest (internal) and a one-line webhook to notify their ops team. Escalation: network-oncall@redwood.com and michael_nw.

opsbot: Ticket TRACK-1234 created: "AcmeCorp POC - outbound access plan" assigned to michael_nw, devon_sec. SLA: 72h initial config.

elaine_s: Next steps for sales playbook: pick one option and send to customer. I suggest we offer them 2 paths: (A) quick: give us 3 EIPs they can open and we map them to a dedicated pool for the POC; (B) secure: enable mTLS and we manage full rotation without them changing allowlist often. Which should I propose as the primary?

michael_nw: Lead with (B) mTLS + short reserved control IP. Call out tradeoffs. If they say "no certs" then fallback to (A). If they need zero touch for POC, propose Private/VPC peering and note a slightly longer lead time.

sasha_reqs: I'll draft the email template and include the curl test + minimal checklist: desired hostnames, desired allowlist CIDR, contact for cert exchange, expected qps. Will loop in finance for POC credits if needed.

elaine_s: Perfect — I'll ping AcmeCorp with options B then A. Thanks all :thumbsup:
